source.prefix_resolved_by: holdings_performance.resolved_prefix(blackdiamond_z09, positions_prefix, firm_scope) -> 45 characters, same as the gold script
source.anchor: schwab/08335338/silver/dim_position/date=YYYY-MM-DD/ (closing_price by cusip; the Schwab own-date close)
source.price: Market Value / Units, rows with Units > 0 and Market Value > 0 and a CUSIP
source.account_key: AccountID, replaced at read time by a one-way digest; used only to group rows, never written

claim_rule: One claim per account-day, by the first row that applies: (1) the account-day holds at least one moved priced row at NEITHER close -> NOT_GRADED (reason neither_row), whatever else it holds; (2) else at least one moved priced row at the PRIOR close -> PRIOR_CLOSE (an account-day holding both own and prior rows and no neither row is PRIOR_CLOSE); (3) else at least one moved priced row and all of them at the own close -> OWN_DATE; (4) else no moved priced row -> NOT_GRADED (reason no_moved_security).  A moved row is a priced row whose security moved on D (anchor close(D) vs close(prior trading day), 1e-4 relative); it is own / prior / neither as in IB-pr-427.  Nothing is dropped: every account present in a graded-day partition has a claim.

mixed_account_days.treatment: own and prior both held, no neither row -> PRIOR_CLOSE; a neither row with any own or prior rows -> NOT_GRADED (neither_row); the two counts overlap when an account-day holds all three (it is NOT_GRADED)

not_graded_split_rule: AMENDMENT 1.  A NOT_GRADED account-day is `ungradeable` when it holds at least one priced security the instrument cannot grade: a priced security the anchor does not carry (outside_anchor), a moved row at neither close (neither_row), or a valued row the instrument cannot price (no_cusip: Units > 0 and Market Value > 0 and no CUSIP; negative_position: Units < 0 and Market Value < 0) -- the last two are kinds the face did not list, named here because such a row could sit on the wrong date; otherwise `nothing_to_grade`.  An account-day holding both kinds is ungradeable, named by the first kind that applies in the order neither_row, outside_anchor, no_cusip, negative_position (the kinds held are all counted in not_graded_holdings_breakdown).  nothing_to_grade classes name the kinds held (cash = Cash Equivalent flag, did_not_move, no_priced_row); an account-day holding more than one kind carries the joined name.

not_graded_split_two_kinds_only.note: the same split if only the two ungradeable kinds the face names (outside_anchor, neither_row) count; no_cusip and negative_position rows then count as nothing to grade

ng_account_days_holding_each_kind_of_row.note: an account-day can hold several kinds, so these do not sum to the NOT_GRADED total; each counts the NOT_GRADED account-days of that reason that hold at least one row of the kind

kinds_defined.cash: row flagged Cash Equivalent = true that is not a graded moved row (priced or not)
kinds_defined.did_not_move: priced row, security carried by the anchor on D and the prior trading day, did not move
kinds_defined.outside_anchor: priced row, security not carried by the anchor on D or on the prior trading day, not flagged cash-equivalent
kinds_defined.no_cusip: valued row (Units > 0 and Market Value > 0) with no CUSIP, not flagged cash-equivalent: the instrument cannot match it to the anchor.  A kind the face did not list; counted as ungradeable
kinds_defined.negative_position: valued row with Units < 0 and Market Value < 0, not flagged cash-equivalent: the instrument's Units > 0 filter leaves it out.  A kind the face did not list; counted as ungradeable
kinds_defined.no_price: any other row the instrument does not price (null or zero Units / Market Value), not flagged cash-equivalent
kinds_defined.cash_priced_outside_anchor: a cash-equivalent-flagged row that is priced and outside the anchor; counted as cash (nothing to grade)

accounts_never_graded_on_a_moved_securit.basis: accounts with no moved priced row on any graded day (IB-pr-427's no_moved_rows).  Each is classed once over its 85 days: if on any day it held a priced security outside the anchor -> holds_outside_anchor_on_some_day; else a valued row with no CUSIP -> holds_no_cusip_valued_row_on_some_day; else a negative position -> holds_negative_position_on_some_day; else the set of kinds it held on any day (cash, did_not_move, no_priced_row).

serving_rule.description: AS WRITTEN (CTO msg 4825): eligible = present today and on the prior graded day; served when today and the prior trading day both read OWN_DATE; blank otherwise, with the reason taken in the order today_PRIOR_CLOSE, today_NOT_GRADED, yesterday_PRIOR_CLOSE, yesterday_NOT_GRADED (the first that applies).

first_day_treatment.treatment: The prior partition of the first graded day (2026-06-09) is ungraded, so no claim exists for it.  The 707 account-days of 2026-06-10 are NOT eligible and are outside the serving counts (they are still claimed and counted in account_days).  Eligible account-days are those present today and on the prior GRADED day.

per_account_served_share_distribution.basis: per account, 100 * served / eligible account-days, over accounts with eligible days

serving_rule_alternative_two_kinds_only.description: NOT THE RULE IN FORCE.  The alternative above, counting as ungradeable only the two kinds the face names (outside_anchor, neither_row); a valued row with no CUSIP or a negative position counts as nothing to grade.  A sensitivity.

serving_rule_alternative.description: NOT THE RULE IN FORCE (CTO's ruling of msg 4825 is HELD, msg 4833).  The alternative the CTO describes: an account-day is good when it reads OWN_DATE or is nothing_to_grade; a return is served when today and the prior trading day are both good.  Same eligible set.  Blank reasons in the order today_PRIOR_CLOSE, today_ungradeable, yesterday_PRIOR_CLOSE, yesterday_ungradeable.

instrument_input_timing.note: Object LastModified from list_objects_v2, times only.  A LastModified is the last write of the object, so a later rewrite of an old day shows the rewrite time; the recent days are the least affected.

instrument_daily_needs.need: The claim stamped for the same account on the prior trading day p (the serving rule reads yesterday's claim)

binding_need: The Cottonwood holdings partition for day D (need 1).  It lands about two hours after the anchor's close for D, which lands the same morning; the prior-day inputs and the calendar are already in place.  A claim for D can be stamped no earlier than that partition.
